wikipedia.title: List of tallest buildings in Chicago

records.Skyline of Chicago: Chicago skyline in 2024 on the shores of Lake Michigan
records.Skyline of Chicago.1: Chicago skyline in 2024 on the shores of Lake Michigan

records.Name: Willis Tower
records.Notes: Formerly known as Sears Tower, a name it is still commonly called today; 3rd-tallest building in the United States, 26th-tallest building in the world; tallest building in the world from 1974 until 1998. Also the tallest building in the Midwest. Tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1970s.[7][8]

records.Name: Trump International Hotel and Tower
records.Notes: 7th-tallest building in the United States; tallest building completed in Chicago in the 2000s. A mixed-use residential and hotel skyscraper.[78]

records.Name: St. Regis Chicago
records.Notes: Formerly known as the Wanda Vista Tower; 11th-tallest building in the United States, and the tallest skyscraper in the world designed by a woman. It is the newest supertall skyscraper in Chicago. Tallest building completed in Chicago in the 2020s. A mixed-use residential and hotel skyscraper.[79][80]

records.Name: Aon Center
records.Notes: 12th-tallest building in the U.S.; formerly known as the Standard Oil Building. Was the tallest building in Chicago before being surpassed by the Willis Tower.[81]

records.Name: 875 North Michigan Avenue
records.Notes: Previously known as John Hancock Center; 13th-tallest building in the United States; tallest building completed in the world in the 1960s; first building in the world outside of New York City to rise at least 1,000 feet (305 m). A mixed-use residential and office skyscraper. Was the tallest building in Chicago before being surpassed by the Aon Center.[82]

records.Name: Franklin Center
records.Notes: Formerly known as the AT&T Corporate Center; 27th-tallest building in the United States; tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1980s.[83][84]

records.Name: Two Prudential Plaza
records.Notes: 30th-tallest building in the United States; tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1990s.[85][86]

records.Name: One Chicago East Tower
records.Notes: 37th-tallest building in the United States. Topped out in July 2021.[87][88]

records.Name: 311 South Wacker Drive
records.Notes: 39th-tallest building in the United States.[89][90]

records.Name: NEMA Chicago
records.Notes: Tallest apartment building in Chicago. Tallest building completed in Chicago in the 2010s.[91][92]

records.Name: 900 North Michigan
records.Notes: A mixed-use skyscraper with office, residential, and hotel components.[93][94]

records.Name: Chase Tower
records.Notes: Also known as First National Plaza. Replaced the Morrison Hotel, the tallest building to ever have been demolished in Chicago. Tallest building in Chicago briefly in 1969, before being surpassed by 875 North Michigan Avenue.[95]

records.Name: Water Tower Place
records.Notes: Currently a mixed-use skyscraper with residential and retail components and a Ritz-Carlton hotel.[96]

records.Name: Aqua
records.Notes: Currently the second-tallest building in the world designed by a female-led architectural firm; first skyscraper in Chicago to contain a hotel, condominiums, apartments and retail space.[97][98][99]

records.Name: 400 Lake Shore Drive North Tower
records.Notes: Approved on December 14, 2020. Groundbreaking ceremony was held in June 2024.[100][101] Construction reached 38th floor in July 2025.[102] Topped off in April 2026.

records.Name: Park Tower
records.Notes: A mixed-use residential and hotel skyscraper.[103][104]

records.Name: Salesforce Tower Chicago
records.Notes: Formerly known as Wolf Point South Tower.[106][107][108]

records.Name: 1000M
records.Notes: Construction was temporarily halted in June 2020 due to funding issues and COVID-19 concerns; a revised design received city approval in June 2021 and construction resumed in December 2021. Topped out in July 2023.[113][114][115][116][117]

records.Name: Three First National Plaza
records.Notes: Also known by its address, 70 West Madison.[120][121]

records.Name: Grant Thornton Tower
records.Notes: Also known by its address, 161 North Clark.[122][123]

records.Name: Blue Cross Blue Shield Tower
records.Notes: The building was originally built in 1997 at 33 stories and a height of 411 feet (125.3 m). In 2010, 21 floors were added in a vertical expansion, along with 3 below-ground floors.[124][125][126]

records.Name: Olympia Centre
records.Notes: Mixed-use office and residential skyscraper.[128][129][130]

records.Name: 150 North Riverside
records.Notes: Tallest building in the city west of the Chicago River.[137]

records.Name: 330 North Wabash
records.Notes: Also known as the IBM Building, and formerly as AMA Plaza. Originally an office building. Currently a mixed-use office and hotel skyscraper.[138][139]

records.Name: Waldorf Astoria Chicago
records.Notes: Mixed-use residential and hotel building.[140][141]

records.Name: One Magnificent Mile
records.Notes: Mixed-use office and residential building.[148][149]

records.Name: 77 West Wacker Drive
records.Notes: Formerly known as the United Building and the R.R. Donnelley Building.[152][153]

records.Name: One North Wacker
records.Notes: Also known as the UBS Tower.[156][157]

records.Name: Richard J. Daley Center
records.Notes: Tallest flat-roofed building in the world that contains fewer than 40 floors. Was the tallest building in Chicago before being surpassed by Chase Tower.[158][159]

records.Name: Lake Point Tower
records.Notes: The only tower in the city that sits on the east side of Lake Shore Drive.[162][163]

records.Name: OneEleven
records.Notes: Formally 111 W. Wacker and Waterview Tower.[174]

records.Name: Chicago Place
records.Notes: Mixed-use residential and office building.[182][183]

records.Name: Chicago Board of Trade Building
records.Notes: One of the tallest Art Deco buildings in the world; tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1930s. Was the tallest building in Chicago before being surpassed by the Richard J. Daley Center.[184][185]

records.Name: One Prudential Plaza
records.Notes: Tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1950s.[186][187]

records.Name: The Clare
records.Notes: An independent-living community for seniors[197][198]

records.Name: Marina City I
records.Notes: Marina City was the first building in the United States to be constructed with the Linden climbing tower cranes. It was also the first post-war urban high-rise residential complex in the United States. The two towers were both the tallest residential and tallest concrete structures in the world upon completion in 1968.[201][202][203]

records.Name: Marina City II
records.Notes: Marina City was the first building in the United States to be constructed with the Linden climbing tower cranes. It was also the first post-war urban high-rise residential complex in the United States. The two towers were both the tallest residential and tallest concrete structures in the world upon completion in 1968.[204][205][206]

records.Name: Mid-Continental Plaza
records.Notes: Also known by its address, 55 East Monroe. Mixed-use office and residential skyscraper.[208][209]

records.Name: Crain Communications Building
records.Notes: Also known by its address, 150 North Michigan Avenue.[210][211]

records.Name: One Chicago West Tower
records.Notes: Also known as 23 West Chicago Avenue.[87][218]

records.Name: Axis Apartments
records.Notes: Formerly known as the Onterie Center. Originally an office tower.[223][224]

records.Name: Loews Hotel Tower
records.Notes: Mixed-use hotel and residential skyscraper.[225]

records.Name: Chicago Temple Building
records.Notes: Tallest building completed in Chicago in the 1920s. Was the tallest building in Chicago before being surpassed by the Chicago Board Of Trade Building.[226][227]

records.Name: Boeing International Headquarters
records.Notes: Also known as the Boeing Building or by its address, 100 North Riverside Plaza. Was the headquarters of Boeing from 2001 to 2022.[234][235]

records.Name: Civic Opera House
records.Notes: Most of the 45-story building is office space. The lower floors house a performance space that is the second-largest opera auditorium in North America, after the Metropolitan Opera House.[241]

records.Name: Atwater Apartments
records.Notes: Also known as Streeter Place.[244][245]

records.Name: Field Building
records.Notes: Originally an office building, now a mixed-use office and residential building.[253]

records.Name: Arrive Michigan Avenue
records.Notes: Also known as The Paragon.[261]

records.Name: Kemper Building
records.Notes: Also known as the United Insurance Building, or Unitrin Building.[262]

records.Name: Mather Tower
records.Notes: Also known as Club Quarters River Hotel[263]

records.Name: 30 South Wacker
records.Notes: Also known as "the Merc"; part of the Chicago Mercantile Exchange Center.[264]

records.Name: 151 North Franklin
records.Notes: In June 2018, 151 North Franklin became the new corporate headquarters for CNA Insurance, which has been headquartered in the Chicago Loop since 1900. CNA Insurance was previously located at 333 South Wabash.[267]

records.Name: 425 South Financial Place
records.Notes: Also known as One Financial Place[269]

records.Name: Park Tower Condominiums
records.Notes: Not to be confused with Park Tower. Also known as 5415 North Sheridan.[273]

records.Name: 600 North Lake Shore Drive – South Tower
Harris Bank Addition II
records.Notes: Officially renamed to the Jesse White State of Illinois building in 2025.[276][277]

records.Name: 321 North Clark
records.Notes: Also known as Quaker Tower.[278]

records.Name: Carbide & Carbon Building
records.Notes: Now a hotel known as Pendry Chicago.[280]

records.Name: 10 South LaSalle
records.Notes: Formerly known under several names, including Chemical Plaza, Manufacturers Hanover Plaza, and Chase Plaza.[283]

records.Name: 727 West Madison
records.Notes: Also known as 1 South Halsted.[289]

records.Name: 55 West Monroe
records.Notes: Also known as the Xerox Center.[290]

records.Name: PNC Center
records.Notes: Also known as One North Franklin[295]

records.Name: Morrisons Hotel
records.Notes: Was the tallest hotel in Chicago until its demolition. First building outside of New York City to have more than 40 floors. The hotel first opened in 1915, with the tower added during an expansion in 1925. It was demolished in 1965. The Chase Tower was later built on the site.[301]

records.Name: Halsted Pointe Phase 1
records.Notes: This initial phase will consist of a 46-story tower designed by local architecture firm HPA. The skyscraper will be anchored by a five-story podium, which will meet the slope of Halsted as it descends from the nearby bridge. Construction started in April 2026. The project has a 24-month timeline.[302]

records.Name: 7 South Dearborn
records.Notes: One South Dearborn was built on the site instead.[303][304]

records.Name: Chicago Spire
records.Notes: 400 Lake Shore Drive is the existing proposal for the site.[305][306]

records.Name: Old Chicago Main Post Office Twin Towers
records.Notes: Part of the Old Chicago Main Post Office Redevelopment pursued by Bill Davies.[307]

records.Name: Thompson Center Redevelopment
records.Notes: Thompson Center is acquired by Alphabet Inc. and is being renovated to become Google's new Midwest HQ.[308][309]

records.Name: Waterview Tower
records.Notes: The original design for Waterview Tower was cancelled after construction of the first 26 floors of the building. OneEleven was built on the vacated structure.[310][311][312]
